rationale: Correct Fatbeam in place. Basalt's fourth flagship fund, Basalt IV, announced the acquisition on March 27, 2023, and the Oregon regulator filing shows Project Lighthouse AIV Feeder LP acquired all Fatbeam Holdings interests effective May 31, 2023. The current Basalt III vehicle label is unsupported. Preserve one active Basalt owner and describe the disclosed chain without inferring Basalt's own economic percentage. Add the verified Fatbeam Holdings / Fatbeam, LLC aliases, official website and Coeur d'Alene headquarters; date current and 2023 scale separately; and replace the announcement-only milestone with a combined signing/closing milestone. SDC and founder ownership remain historical seller context rather than an additional manager-universe OwnershipPeriod. No later sale, ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Fatbeam is a Coeur d'Alene, Idaho-based owner-operator of fiber networks serving commercial, education, healthcare, government, carrier, tower, residential and multifamily customers across Arizona, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Washington and Wyoming. Its services include dedicated internet access, Ethernet private line, wavelength, dark fiber, wireless backup, tower and data-center connectivity, managed Wi-Fi, cyber/cloud and residential fiber/wireless. Fatbeam's current network page reports 1,600+ on-net buildings, 150,000+ total fiber miles and 150+ cities across eight states; Basalt's current portfolio page reports 1,250 route miles. A June 2023 regulator filing separately reported 1,252 route miles, 13 metro markets, 128,000+ strand miles and over 40 cities. Basalt IV announced an agreement to acquire Fatbeam on March 27, 2023, and Project Lighthouse AIV Feeder LP acquired all Fatbeam Holdings interests effective May 31, 2023. Fatbeam remains in Basalt's current portfolio, and no later ownership transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.
